Improve the capacity of businesses to integrate into domestic and international markets through increases in productivity and improvements in corporate governance and the development and application of modern technology and marketing practices. Enhance the capacity of businesses and business associations in terms of their corporate governance capabilities and their application of best practices and technologies to achieve increased production and marketing of products and services. It includes adoption of efficient production processes, improved labor productivity, environmentally-sound management of natural resources and the development of accounting and management systems that can help the company and industry group implement business, labor, product and process standards that enhance business competitiveness. Business capacity development programs may include activities that help men- and women-owned firms and associations respond to these international markets and create regional alliances.

title.narrative: Ethiopian Sheep and Goat Productivity Improvement Project

description.narrative: The Ethiopia Sheep and Goat Productivity Improvement Program (ESGPIP) is a USAID- funded five-year project designed to reduce constraints to increased productivity of small ruminants in Ethiopia through appropriate interventions. The ESGPIP supports USAIDs long-term strategic goal of realizing a more peaceful, secure, prosperous, and healthy Ethiopia, as well as strategic objectives of increasing human capacity and social resiliency and private sector-led economic growth.

description.narrative: Improve the ability of the USG, host countries and other partners to prepare for and mitigate the effects of disasters, including both natural disasters and complex emergencies, taking into account the differences in men and womens freedom of movement and access to information. Activities under this component include any efforts to enhance the capacities of the USG (in Washington and in the field), humanitarian assistance providers, national host-country authorities, and local communities to engage in disaster reduction and response activities. Activities consist of standardized and coordinated assessments, monitoring, information sharing, data and situational analysis, joint planning; enhancement of coping mechanisms, including the capacity to address adaptation to constantly changing situations on the ground including climate variability and climate change.

description.narrative: (Ethiopia): The DRM-CB activity aims to save lives and livelihoods by strengthening the capacity and commitment of the DRM system to deliver a more effective, self-financed, and accountable response to humanitarian and climate shocks. The activity is co-financed with the UK Foreign Commonwealth and Development Office..The weakness of Ethiopia's DRM system directly undermines the effectiveness of USAID's development and humanitarian assistance. In 2018, USAID Center for Resilience estimated that having a stronger DRM system could save Ethiopia $965 million over 15 years. In 2022, an estimated 29 million Ethiopians need humanitarian assistance, which is delivered through the decentralized DRM system..The DRM-CB activity provides targeted technical assistance to strengthen the commitment and capacity of the Government of Ethiopia's DRM system at all levels to deliver effective response to shocks. Technical assistance will include improve GOE's financial planning and preparation for disasters, and strengthen the GOE's capacity to improve coordination to implement an effective response. This will increase the GOE's capacity to deliver quality and timely life-saving assistance, reduce the impact of shocks, save lives, safeguard livelihoods, protect development gains and food security, and reduce reliance on humanitarian assistance..By building the capacity of Ethiopia's DRM institutions and assisting them to plan and prepare for shocks, DRM-CB will improve the quality and timeliness of responses to shocks that negatively impact health and nutrition, and prevent spikes in acute malnutrition and other shock-related morbidity. It will support health system capacity to maintain effective delivery of nutrition services, including management of wasting in children under five and infant and young child feeding in emergencies, and improve monitoring nutritional risk and adaptation of interventions to address drivers of risk. .........

description.narrative: Despite the improvements through ELTAP, many technical and policy challenges remained that are targeted under the follow-on ELAP project. The ELAP project further strengthens rural land tenure security by: Component 1: Strengthening the Legal Framework on Land Administration including undertaking legal assessments and workshops; legal review, consultation and development; and training and capacity building in areas of primarily sedenary agriculture (Amhara, Oromia, SNNP and Tigray regions) and pastoral agriculture (Afar and Somali regions). Component 2: Promoting Tenure Security to Enhance Investment in Land including refining methodologies for registration/cadastral surveying; organizating registration teams and providing support for regional land agencies; supporting delivery of land certification/registration and issuance of certificates; cadastral survey and mapping, and training of trainers. Component 3: Increasing Public Information and Awareness of land rights in both areas of sedenary agriculture (Amhara, Oromia, SNNP and Tigray regions) and pastoral agriculture (Afar and Somali regions). Strengthening Capacity of Federal and Regional Land Administration Agencies to Conduct Land Reform and Deliver Land Administration Services including facilitating donor coordination, and establishing Memorandums of Understanding with GOE and donors to promote property rights reform and strengthen land administration. ARD works in collaboration with the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development (MoARD) and the Regional Land Administration Agencies (RLAs) of six regional states: Afar, Amhara, Oromia, Southern Nations, Nationalities, and Peoples (SNNP), Somali, and Tigray. Other partner institutions such as the Ethiopian Mapping Agency (EMA), universities and research institutions, and private sector are engaged in specific training, public awareness, and research services.

Assist special populations which may be vulnerable or at-risk on a temporary or chronic basis whose needs are not addressed under emergency humanitarian assistance or other programs. These include groups such as the disabled; orphans, children and at-risk youth; victims of trafficking; victims of gender-based violence; refugees, returnees, ethnic minorities, internally displaced or other socially excluded groups; the elderly; and female heads of household. Depending on circumstances, services may intend to protect groups; mitigate adverse conditions they face, or to remove barriers to help integrate them into society. title.narrative: Joint Technical Cooperation Program in Smallholder Horticulture (Phase -IV) - MASHAV

description.narrative: (Ethiopia): The Smallholder Horticulture Program is a partnership with the Israeli development agency and the Government of Ethiopia to promote economic growth in rural areas by strengthening the commercialization of smallholder farmers in horticulture production. This partnership effectively leverages funding and technical expertise from another donor to improve the avocado industry in Ethiopia. Avocados are an important crop for both income and nutrition, with dramatically growing domestic and international demand. By training farmers, extension agents, nursery managers, and district Agriculture and Natural Resource officers in everything from Good Agricultural Practices to marketing and certification, the activity is driving better incomes for farmers and increased availability of a nutritious food for consumers, both important to the Feed the Future objectives of reducing poverty and improving nutrition.

The Health Sector Financing Reform (HSFR) project has been assisting the government of Ethiopia with implementing the hospital and health center revenue retention and utilization policy and other reforms for more than a decade. These include a fee waiver system that ensures the poor can access health services and the opening of private wings in hospitals to generate revenue and help retain health professionals.

description.narrative: Assist special populations which may be vulnerable or at-risk on a temporary or chronic basis whose needs are not addressed under emergency humanitarian assistance or other programs. These include groups such as the disabled; orphans, children and at-risk youth; victims of trafficking; victims of gender-based violence; refugees, returnees, ethnic minorities, internally displaced or other socially excluded groups; the elderly; and female heads of household. Depending on circumstances, services may intend to protect groups; mitigate adverse conditions they face, or to remove barriers to help integrate them into society. Components may include measures to increase the capacity of local service and advocacy NGOs and/or professional social workers; to establish public/private service delivery partnerships as well as family and community focused service models; to establish effective referral networks; to develop appropriate service protocols and methods for screening prospective recipients; or to improve public understanding and sensitivity to the needs of the vulnerable. While services provided should not exclude victims of trafficking in persons, programs designed specifically for this group fall under the Peace and Security Objective under the Transnational Crime Area and the Trafficking in Persons and Migrant Smuggling Element.

title.narrative: Ethiopia General Education Quality Improvement Project II

description.narrative: The development objective of the Second Phase of General Education Quality Improvement Project for Ethiopia is to improve learning conditions in primary and secondary schools and strengthen institutions at different levels of educational administration. The project has six components. The first component is curriculum, textbooks, assessment, examinations, and inspection. This component will support improvement of learning conditions in grades KG-12 by providing increased access to teaching and learning materials and through improvements to the curriculum by assessing the strengths and weaknesses of the current curriculum. This component has following four sub-components: (i) curriculum reform and implementation; (ii) teaching and learning materials; (iii) assessment and examinations; and (iv) inspection. The second component is teacher development program (TDP). This component will support improvements in learning conditions in both primary and secondary schools by advancing the quality of teaching in general education through: (a) enhancing the training of pre-service teachers in teacher education institutions; and (b) improving the quality of in-service teacher training. This component has following three sub-components: (i) pre-service teacher training; (ii) in-service teacher training; and (iii) licensing and relicensing of teachers and school leaders. The third component is school improvement plan. This component will support the strengthening of school planning in order to improve learning outcomes, and to partly fund the school improvement plans through school grants. It has following two sub-components: (i) school improvement plan; and (ii) school grants. The fourth component is management and capacity building, including education management information systems (EMIS). This component will support management and capacity building aspect of the project.

title.narrative: MDTF for World Bank for Ethiopia

description.narrative: MDTF for World Bank for Ethiopia

(Ethiopia): .The Multi Donor Initiative (MDI) was launched in 2014 in order to harmonize and leverage donor activities and resources towards building a more dynamic and competitive private sector in Ethiopia. MDI Pillar II will directly address access to finance issues, with a particular emphasis on Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) in the agriculture sector. The planned activities of the MDI will include needed technical support for Ethiopia to introduce and/or expand commodity based financing (important for producers), movable collateral and leasing (important for agricultural machinery), and mobile money (important for smallholders) among other legal and regulatory reforms that are needed. FY 2016 resources will provide the second $1 million increment of USAID's pledged support..

title.narrative: Productive Safety Net IV, Ethiopia Partnership Multi-donor Trust Fund

description.narrative: Productive Safety Net IV, Ethiopia Partnership Multi-donor Trust Fund

title.narrative: Agriculture Growth Program (AGP) II Multi Donor Trust Fund

description.narrative: (Ethiopia): The Agricultural Growth Project Multi Donor Trust Fund, administered by World Bank, will enable the Government of Ethiopia to improve its capacity to research, design, manage, and evaluate agriculture and nutrition related activities conducted within the scope of the Agriculture Growth Project II (APG II). This is the only major multi-donor platform that brings together key development partners and provides a financing and technical vehicle for effective and coordinated engagement to improve implementation of the AGP itself.. .USAID's support under the trust fund focuses on improving the business-enabling environment in Ethiopia, particularly for small and medium enterprises in crop and livestock value chains. This activity aligns with the upcoming new Strategic Framework.

Agriculture is the science and practice of food, feed, and fiber production (including forestry, wildlife, fisheries, aquaculture and floraculture) and its relationships to natural resources, processing, marketing, distribution, utilization (including nutrition), and trade.

Ethiopias Productive Safety Net Program (PSNP) is a large national social safety net (SSN) program that responds not only to chronic food insecurity among Ethiopia's poor, but also to shorter-term shocks, mainly droughts. It targets a highly climate-vulnerable population, offering a practical model of how SSNs can be designed to meet the social protection needs of the most vulnerable, while simultaneously reducing the risks from disaster and climate-related impacts.

Improve sustainability of a productive and clean environment by reducing risks to the health of the workforce and the population in general, communities, and ecosystems from environmental pollution and other environmental risks associated with industrial and agricultural production, urbanization, energy use, transport, and other human activity.

Support and strengthen the negotiation process and implement peace and reconciliation processes, accords and ceasefire agreements at track levels 1, 2 and 3, including support to indigenous peacebuilding efforts. For a peace/negotiations process to have a chance of success, it must entail building trust in the process, between parties, and among their constituents, with a special focus on including women. Illustrative activities include negotiation training; platform development; public opinion polling; facilitation activities; elder statesmen engagement; provision of international expert advice and knowledge; financial support to parties; multi-stakeholder dialogues; assistance with the design of peacebuilding training programs; support and maintenance of agreed verification mechanisms; support to complaint tracking mechanisms; and work with local and national government representatives to bring them closer to their constituencies.

description.narrative: (Ethiopia): .FY 2018 Family Planning funds.will be used to buy into the PEPFAR mechanism to support comprehensive family.planning for hard to reach key populations, i.e., female sex workers and.adolescent girls and women engaged in transaction sex. This service will be.provided in the community using existing platforms such as drop in centers. These venues are.providing confidential services only to female sex workers. Specifically,.the funds will facilitate peer demand creation, training for service providers,.peer educators and other support staffs, to conduct regular site level.mentoring, etc. .

description.narrative: (Ethiopia): READ II's goal is to improve the.reading proficiency and educational attainment of 15 million children in order.to lead them to productive lives and drive Ethiopia's economic, social, and.political development. READ II interventions directly support the Agency's.strategic focus on literacy by equipping teachers with effective early grade.reading instruction techniques and grade appropriate materials in seven local.languages and English. .FY2020 funds will provide students.in the six target regions with a learning-supportive environment in schools,.communities, and homes. Through technical assistance, USAID will improve.the usability of the training materials to make early grade literacy materials.more responsive and adaptable to teacher and classroom exigencies, enhance teacher.training and professional development programs, increase the engagement between.youth and parents with the schools, and improve the leadership and management.capacity of school administrators to provide support and guidance to teachers..In addition, READ II will address school-related gender-based violence through.the implementation of a radio drama focused on empowering students to persevere.in their education and in life despite societal and gender barriers. .Furthermore, to ensure that.students' access to education and learning is not interrupted given ongoing.unrest and shocks such as the global COVID-19 public health emergency, READ II.will support and build the capacity of MOE structures and schools to i).identify crisis triggers, ii) develop crisis response plans, iii) establish.early warning systems, iv) mobilize and manage resources, and vii) advocate for.the MOE to establish a permanent Education in Emergency unit. This activity.contributes to Development Objective 4 of USAID/Ethiopia's CDCS (Sustained.Improvements in Essential Service Delivery). .... ...

description.narrative: (Ethiopia): The Malaria Diagnosis and Treatment Activity improves the quality of malaria diagnosis and treatment services in both public and private health facilities. The activity will strengthen partnerships and coordination at national and regional levels; strengthen and scale up quality assurance (QA) systems for malaria diagnosis and treatment; improve infrastructure (minor renovation) and human resource capacity for malaria diagnosis and case management...MDTA will expand its implementation to facilities in 30 districts in Somali Region and additional 23 districts from Oromia and Amhara regions, bringing the total number of districts to 203.....

title.narrative: Feed the Future Livelihoods for Resilience Learning Activity

description.narrative: The Livelihoods for Resilience (L4R) program operates in four highland regions of Ethiopia to support and enhance livelihood opportunities for chronically food insecure households. USAID launched the L4R Learning Activity to provide data for assessing outputs, outcomes, overall impact, and performance of the five-year L4R program. The baseline study provides an evidence base against which to monitor and assess the progress and effectiveness of L4R interventions during and after the program. It also supports a robust learning and adapting agenda and a related research agenda.

(Ethiopia): The Health Financing Improvement Program (HFIP) strengthens health financing functions and systems to support Universal Health Coverage of essential health care for Ethiopian citizens by reducing financial barriers through institutionalizing different Health Care Financing (HCF) reforms. USAID, through this activity, works to increase domestic resource mobilization (DRM) for health, financial risk-protection programs (Community-Based Health Insurance (CBHI) and Social Health Insurance), and improve local capacity for better decision-making and resource management. With FY 2021 funds, among others, HFIP will focus on further widening of the CBHI coverage in rural areas, rollout of the CBHI program to urban cities, scaling-up in low-land/developing regions, primarily for PF programs and other Public Health Programs like MCH. Extra effort will also be exerted to mitigate the impact of COVID-19 and other shocks the country is experiencing and maintain CBHI memberships and new enrollments..These efforts directly support Ethiopia's Integrated Country Strategy Mission Goal 3: Spur Broad-based Economic Growth and Mission Objective 3.3: Ethiopia Increases Utilization of Quality Health Services and Improves Capacity to Prevent and Manage Pandemic and Epidemic Health Threats...... .

description.narrative: (Ethiopia): .FETEH is a two-year activity that will provide flexible and rapid response technical assistance to the Attorney General's Office (AGO), relevant sub-committees within the AGO, the Federal Supreme Court of Ethiopia (FSCE), appropriate committees in Parliament, and/or other related government ministries in the reform process. The activity will make grants to civil society organizations and media to ensure public input into the democratic reform process, improving citizen engagement and public consultation of proposed changes to Ethiopia's legal and judicial framework. Specifically, FETEH will:.a. Build the capacity of the AGO, its 14-person Council, its legal drafting sub-committees, FSCE and other rule of law actors to adopt and implement legal and judicial reform consistent with international human rights norms..b. Support the ability of civil society organizations and the media to engage the AGO and the legal drafting sub-committees on legal and judicial reforms..c. Support the appropriate committees in Parliament to ensure that they develop sufficient capacity to approve the adoption of legal reforms...d. Support the FSCE with improving Ethiopia's court management system... ..Establishing and solidifying the root of Ethiopia's ability to enforce the rule of law is a critical means through which Ethiopia can maintain transparency, openness, and stability. Without accountability, fair and just laws, transparency, and access to justice, conflict brews. The new Ethiopian Government is in a sensitive time of transition by which triggers such as conflict are highly de-stabilizing and harmful to promising, western-leaning reforms. ... .

description.narrative: (Ethiopia): Land remains a very important factor of production for pastoralists, smallholder farmers, and small entrepreneurs to escape poverty and food insecurity. Secure land tenure enables landholders to make longer-term investments into farming and agri-businesses, thereby contributing to increased productivity and incomes. It also allows pastoralists and farmers to lease their landholdings to entrepreneurs who need land to grow their businesses. In addition to helping landholders build more lucrative and stable livelihoods and move out of poverty, these leasing arrangements also have a spillover effect on the rural economy by increasing opportunities for high growth potential small and medium enterprises to provide services and employment opportunities. ..Building on USAID/Ethiopia's previous investments to improve rural landholders', and particularly women's, land tenure security, the Feed the Future Ethiopia Land Governance Activity will work with customary institutions, rural landholders, and urban dwellers to adopt a scalable approach for land demarcation and certification. The approach includes the use of satellite imagery, simple and cost-effective land surveying and mapping tools, an integrated land information database, research, training, and professional services. The activity will work with key civil society organizations, such as the Ethiopia Land Administration Professionals Association, to improve the rights of landholders through increased advocacy, research, and technical assistance for land surveying, planning, demarcation, and registration. The activity's gender-sensitive approaches significantly improve women's tenure security and economic empowerment...By improving incomes and food security, social cohesion, and more equitable urbanization, the activity advances the USG Global Food Security Strategy......

title.narrative: Engineering Services and Construction Oversight- Phase 2

description.narrative: (Ethiopia): The objective of this task order (TO) is to provide professional engineering and other technical services to USAID/Ethiopia and USAID/Djibouti to design and manage the infrastructure components of the Mission's portfolio, thereby ensuring cost-effectiveness, development impact, and sustainability, as well as reduction of risk to the Mission. Initial services under this TO are primarily for planning and design reviews, construction oversight, and monitoring and evaluation of ongoing Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) and health center renovation/construction activities. Other services under this TO could include conducting analyses and assessments, planning, design, procurement support, construction oversight, commissioning, monitoring and evaluation, capacity building, community engagement, technical consultancy, and general management and administration for other infrastructure activities across the Mission's portfolio. FY2021 funds will be used for the engineering service and construction oversight of all WASH activities (i.e., Urban WASH, Climate Resilient WASH, Market Based Sanitation & Hygiene, etc.). .These efforts also directly support Ethiopia's ICS Mission Goal 3: Spur Broad-based Economic Growth and Mission Objective 3.3: Ethiopia Increases Utilization of Quality Health Services and Improves Capacity to Prevent and Manage Pandemic and Epidemic Health Threats....... .. .. .. .... .

(Ethiopia): .The goal of this activity is to strengthen democratic.institutions and processes to advance and safeguard democratic reforms and.principles in Ethiopia. This goal will be achieved by (1) promoting the.meaningful participation of all citizens, including women, youth, and other.traditionally marginalized groups; (2) promoting the integrity of elections as.a sustainable vehicle for choosing leaders peacefully and democratically; (3).Harnessing the comparative advantages of media and technology to promote.citizen understanding and engagement and transparent political competition; and.(4) promoting competitive and representative multiparty political systems. This.activity directly supports Ethiopia's Journey to Self-Reliance given the.potential far reaching impacts of establishing and institutionalizing.democratic governance systems and opening space among civil society actors -.precursors to more effective governance structures and therefore greater sustainability.of development interventions. Democratic Governance systems that Ethiopians.trust is one that will also deter potentially de-stabilizing conflict, which.would wreak havoc on the stability of the rest of the region - An American.foreign policy objective. ..USAID will provide beneficiaries.with information, knowledge, skills, and technology to foster transparent,.participatory, and competitive election processes and promote citizen-driven.engagement. Examples include sharing standards-based democratic practices drawn.from the U.S. as well as global networks like the Global Network of.Domestic Election Monitors, sharing and disseminating information.through public opinion research and empirical studies and assessments, and.piloting new approaches to citizen engagement and responsive party.representation. USAID will also support the NEBE, civil society, media, and political parties to engage the public in.ways that elevate citizen information access and emphasize the need for public.feedback...

description.narrative: (Ethiopia): Resilience in Pastoral Areas South (RiPA South) builds resilience capacities of households and communities, promotes peace and stability, and increases trade and investment opportunities for local micro, small and medium enterprises. .RIPA South is improving the resilience capacities of households, communities, and local governance institutions in 16 districts in the Oromia, SNNPR, and Somali Regions of Ethiopia, increasing food security for over 107,533 households..Using FY 2022 funds, RiPA South will assist district and village Disaster Risk Management Committees to implement disaster risk management plans by training trainers on disaster risk preparedness; supporting women's empowerment groups to strengthen savings, lending, and social support; and improving access to water for people and livestock. The activity will also continue providing advisory service to businesses, improve community access to livestock and crop price information, improve access to finance for businesses, and support food and feed seed production and marketing enterprises. .RiPA South will also continue to use a family health approach (FHA) to target children under five during the first 1,000 days of life. Through these FHA groups, RiPA South will engage mothers, fathers , and grandmothers to influence health, nutrition, and hygiene related behaviors. FY 2022 funds will be used to disseminate context-specific social and behavior change communication materials through local media..... .

sector.narrative: Water supply and sanitation - large systems

description.narrative: (Ethiopia): Resilience in Pastoral Areas North (RiPA North) improves the resilience capacities of households, markets, and local institutions across 22 target districts in the Somali, Afar, and Oromia regions of Ethiopia. The activity contributes to enhanced food security and inclusive economic growth for over 178,000 households. FY 2022 funds will continue to strengthen disaster risk management systems and capabilities of communities and local governments through training, technical advice, and institutional support. The activity will facilitate two-way early warning and response information flow between communities and local governments at regional, district, and community-levels. The activity will also catalyze inclusive and effective labor markets and a dynamic private sector to improve economic and employment opportunities for youth and women. The activity increases productivity and marketing of livestock and crop systems by strengthening rangeland management and improving access to animal health service, water supply, farm inputs, and financial services...RiPA North will continue to promote nutrition-sensitive and nutrition-smart agricultural practices. It will provide social behavior change communication interventions to tackle the multi-dimensional nutrition, sanitation, and hygiene problems that affect health and economic growth of target households. It will promote increased consumption of animal source foods. The activity will also continue to co-lead and facilitate the Ethiopian Civil Society Coalition for Scaling-up Nutrition to strengthen the strategic partnership with other resilience focused programs to scale up nutrition and WASH best practices in target pastoral areas....

Reduce the threat or impact of violent conflict and promote the peaceful resolution of differences, mitigate violence if it has already broken out, or establish a framework for peace and reconciliation. description.narrative: (Ethiopia): The USAID Health Workforce Improvement Program (HWIP) improves the quality of education and training for health professionals by focusing on strengthening human resource capacity. HWIP partners with 29 higher education institutions to strengthen the capacity of their faculty to design and teach courses, including digital courses. HWIP supports the expansion of gender-sensitive programs with the goal of increasing the number of women in teaching and leadership roles in these institutions and to promote more women professionals in the health sector overall...HWIP works closely with professional associations to promote continuous quality improvement and accreditation of the academic programs and universities...HWIP provides technical and financial support to 200 primary and secondary health facilities to improve evidence-based human resource planning, recruitment and placement, in-service training, continuing professional development, and improved motivation, retention, and performance of the health workforce... .

description.narrative: (Ethiopia): The USAID Eliminate TB Project (ETBE) provides comprehensive technical support to improve access and utilization of quality TB, drug-resistant TB (DR-TB), and TB/HIV services. With FY 2022 funds, the activity will engage with private health service providers and optimize community-based TB case finding treatment. The activity will also increase access to drug susceptibility testing by expanding the use of rapid TB diagnostic tools and patient-centered TB and DR-TB treatment services and expand treatment for latent TB infection. The activity will strengthen the health systems' referral and care services and strengthen TB research that will inform and guide TB programming...This activity will benefit over 88 million people in six regions of the country: Oromia; Amhara; Southern Nations, Nationalities, and Peoples'; South West Ethiopia Peoples'; Sidama; and Tigray...... . .

title.narrative: Federal Auditor General (OFAG) of Ethiopia Technical Assistance

description.narrative: The purpose of this Agreement is to request for a PASA with United States Government Accountability Office GAO0 to provide an assistance for capacity building for Office of the Federal Auditor General (OFAG) of Ethiopia

(Ethiopia): Ethiopia is a youthful population with more than 70 percent of its population under the age of 30. The demographic challenges are enormous but also can create opportunities. Ethiopian youth are faced with large under-employment and unemployment and have fewer opportunities to grow to their full potential due to the prolonged conflict in the north, drought in the lowlands, economic hardships, and high inflation. These factors in turn create perfect conditions for groups seeking to mobilize youth for violence. ..The Integrated Youth Activity (Kefeta) is a youth-led activity that empowers 15 to 29 year-old youth to advance their own social, economic, and civic development so they productively contribute to the development of their communities and Ethiopia's peace and stability. Kefeta will implement holistic and integrated youth programming directed at secondary cities affected by conflict and drought while preventing violence in other urban areas and maintain much needed stability through engaging youth in peacebuilding and stabilization efforts...Kefeta will build youth resilience, prevent gender-based violence against young women and girls, and provide essential youth-friendly health and financial services. Funds will strengthen youth networks and establish new youth coalitions and youth groups in educational institutions, community settings, and large workplaces to promote sustained dialogue among youth groups. Kefeta also engages the private sector and builds the capacity of youth-serving organizations for sustainable impact beyond the life of the activity. .Kefeta will contribute to USAID youth in development policy goals, supporting U.S. Foreign Policy objectives through engaging youth in promoting peace and stability in times of rapid change, conflict, or crises......

Assist special populations which may be vulnerable or at-risk on a temporary or chronic basis whose needs are not addressed under emergency humanitarian assistance or other programs. These include groups such as the disabled; orphans, children and at-risk youth; victims of trafficking; victims of gender-based violence; refugees, returnees, ethnic minorities, internally displaced or other socially excluded groups; the elderly; and female heads of household. Depending on circumstances, services may intend to protect groups; mitigate adverse conditions they face, or to remove barriers to help integrate them into society. Components may include measures to increase the capacity of local service and advocacy NGOs and/or professional social workers; to establish public/private service delivery partnerships as well as family and community focused service models; to establish effective referral networks; to develop appropriate service protocols and methods for screening prospective recipients; or to improve public understanding and sensitivity to the needs of the vulnerable. While services provided should not exclude victims of trafficking in persons, programs designed specifically for this group fall under the Peace and Security Objective under the Transnational Crime Area and the Trafficking in Persons and Migrant Smuggling Element.

description.narrative: (Ethiopia): The Resilience Learning activity (RLA) supports the Transition into Graduation through Enhanced Highlands Resilience (TIGER) project to be more efficient, effective, and transparent in achieving development and resilience outcomes in the chronically vulnerable highlands of Ethiopia through the use of evidence, adaptive management techniques and Collaborating, Learning and Adapting (CLA) practices. .RL will set the stage for scaling and improving the effectiveness of government systems and programs on climate change adaptation activities leading to reductions in chronic vulnerability in Ethiopia by:.Facilitating coordination and collaboration across TIGER partners.Providing relevant research to the TIGER learning agenda.Provide timely field-based measurement.Ensuring iterative planning and action.Supporting data-driven decision-making and innovation...RL will also measure the impact of layering and sequencing multiple USAID investments. Furthermore, RL will support a stakeholder-wide culture of collaborative recognition of successes and failures. RLA is a learning, collaborating, and adapting mechanism for the activities implemented under the highland's resilience project. These activities aim to increase capacity to sustainably diversify own production; increase last-mile supply of nutritious foods and improve knowledge of maternal, infant and young child nutrition (MIYCN) practices and demand for health services. The collaborative learning and rapid feedback approach of the RL activity is founded on the principles of local ownership and collective impact to support Ethiopia's journey towards self-reliance. The design of the activity supports a stakeholder-wide culture of collaborative recognition of successes, failures, and areas of uncertainty leading to reductions in chronic vulnerability in Ethiopia........

title.narrative: USAID TEKI Activity Fighting Plastic Bags With Sign Language

description.narrative: TEKI is an Amharic word from the verb "Metekat," which means replacing. TEKI Fighting Plastic Bags with Sign Language is a three-year activity funded by USAIDEthiopia and implemented by Teki Paper Bags PLC. The goal of the TEKI activity is to empower youths with disabilities to turn the fight against plastic bag pollution into a national employment-intensive inclusion solution.

title.narrative: Promoting Rights and Inclusion for Disability Empowerment (PRIDE) Activity

description.narrative: Promoting rights and inclusion for disability empowerment (pride) activity

(Ethiopia): Ethiopia has made significant progress in reducing malaria-related morbidity and mortality. Effective surveillance and malaria treatment have been cornerstones of Ethiopia's successful campaign against malaria. ..The Surveillance for Malaria Elimination (S4ME) Activity supports high quality malaria elimination interventions in 67 low and very low malaria transmission districts and health facilities, as well as efforts to strengthen the capacity of healthcare workers' and district administrators' to understand and use data for effective decision making. ..The Activity tests and develops models of effective malaria elimination by helping to identify and manage all malaria cases occurring in districts. The effort is locally driven and focuses on district-level capacity building, especially malaria surveillance systems in health facilities and communities to improve the ability to detect and report malaria cases. The surveillance systems are designed to detect malaria cases even in hard to reach populations, such as refugees, internally displaced persons, and migrants....

title.narrative: Biodiversity and Community Resilience in the Omo Valley

description.narrative: (Ethiopia): The Biodiversity and Community Resilience in the Omo Valley (BIOM) activity increases the resilience of communities and the ecosystem of South Omo, which has undergone a series of major shocks in recent decades. South Omo communities have been affected by major displacements due to the Gibe III dam construction, expanding export agriculture, and escalating conflicts between the state and local groups. The activity will work with indigenous communities to increase their capacity to sustainably manage their biodiversity and to develop community-managed and led approaches to sustainable livelihoods. The activity will improve outcomes for communities by centering them (particularly women and youth) as stewards of the landscape and key organizers of conservation efforts. It will also train and empower locals to engage more directly in the tourist economy. Through privately funded, community-run ecotourism ventures in Tama Wildlife Sanctuary, a Community Conserved Area (CCA), the activity will promote conservation of local biodiversity and increase tourism-based income. BIOM will reduce threats to high biodiversity areas, such as the Omo and Mago National Parks, by promoting diversification of livelihoods and improving access to basic social and economic services. The formalization of the CCA will promote land rights and tenure security for local communities who experience tensions with migrant laborers working in adjacent sugar cane plantations...... .. .

description.narrative: (Ethiopia): The USAID Healthy Behaviors Activity increases sustained adoption of appropriate health and nutrition behaviors to reduce maternal and child mortality. It focuses primarily at the district level and below to ensure communities can act to improve their own health. The activity will promote behavior change to support improved maternal and child health, family planning and reproductive health, nutrition, water hygiene and sanitation (WASH), and infectious disease management, including malaria. ..Based on proven approaches that address drivers for health beliefs and behaviors at the individual, family, and community levels, the Activity will promote social behavior change that supports healthy behaviors and improved health outcomes...The activity increases demand by community members for health services; builds service providers' communication skills for improved patient interactions; supports use of districts and communities' traditional communication platforms for community mobilization and health campaigns; and builds capacity of local organizations to coordinate for gender transformative programming. ..The activity will be implemented in Amhara, Benishangul Gumuz, Gambella, Oromia, Southern Nations, Nationalities and Peoples', and Sidama Regions.......... .

title.narrative: Feed the Future Ethiopia Community Nutrition Activity

description.narrative: Through its Feed the Future initiative, the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) partners with the Government of Ethiopia (GOE) to invest in food security, build resilience, and accelerate economic growth. The Growth through Nutrition activity is USAIDs flagship nutrition and water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) investment, a six-year (2016-2022) project that aims to improve the nutritional status of women, young children, and adolescents in six regional states of Ethiopia (Southern Nations, Nationalities, and Peoples, Oromia, Amhara, Sidama, Southwest Ethiopia Peoples and Tigray regions). The project works across multiple sectors in close coordination with the Ministries of Agriculture; Health; Education; and Water, Irrigation and Energy.
USAID TB local organizations network for key affected and vulnerable population (KAP) activity in developing regional states (DRS).

The Feed the Future Ethiopia Highlands Resilience Activity (HRA) aims to enable 120,000 households in the highland regions of Ethiopia to reach the graduation threshold from the Government of Ethiopia (GoE) Productive Safety Net Program (PSNP5).

description.narrative: The overall objective of USAID Empowered Communities Activity is to achieve better health and nutritional outcomes through improved community ownership of health and strengthened social accountability systems and platforms. The activity will be primarily funded with family planning, and maternal and child health funding. Therefore, all expected results and proposed interventions should contribute to the betterment of the lives of women, children, youth and men ultimately, improved reproductive, maternal, newborn, child and adolescent health and nutrition (RMNCAH-N) outcomes.

Agriculture is the science and practice of food, feed, and fiber production (including forestry, wildlife, fisheries, aquaculture and floraculture) and its relationships to natural resources, processing, marketing, distribution, utilization (including nutrition), and trade.

The USAID Disaster Risk Management (DRM) Activity will work to reduce the impact of shocks in Ethiopia by strengthening DRM planning and preparedness, improving DRM coordination, enhancing resource mobilization and management, and partnering with local organizations to provide locally led, tailored assistance to districts and regions.

The overall purpose of this Activity is to increase gender inclusive and equitable access to, and use of, improved sanitation and hygiene products and services. The Activity will work to fulfill this purpose through four complementary intermediate results: 1. Gender inclusive sanitation and hygiene sector governance strengthened; 2. Increased demand for gender inclusive basic sanitation and hygiene products, services, and behaviors; 3. Increased equitable supply of diverse and affordable basic sanitation and hygiene products; and 4. Improved coordination and learning among sanitation and hygiene actors including the private sector.

title.narrative: Ethiopia Elections and Political Processes Activity (EEPPA)

description.narrative: CEPPS seeks to build political will and institutional capacity for competitive, peaceful elections, as well as inclusive, responsive, democratic governance. To do this, CEPPS works directly with the National Election Board of Ethiopia (NEBE), civil society organizations, media, and political parties, in order to strengthen the participation of all citizens throughout their political systems, including women, youth, and other traditionally marginalized groups. Additionally, CEPPS promotes the integrity of Ethiopian elections to peacefully and democratically select leaders; to better harness the medias capability to promote citizens political understanding, and transparency within the electoral process, as well as to improve competitive, representative multiparty political systems.

The purpose of this activity is to improved learning outcomes, wellbeing, and systems resilience for most vulnerable primary school age children affected by crises in Ethiopia.

The purpose of the USAID/Ethiopia Health Security Activity (HSA) is to reduce the impact of infectious disease outbreaks on morbidity and mortality through building a resilient One Health (OH) surveillance, diagnostics and workforce development capacities. The HSA will achieve this through strengthening Ethiopias capacity to detect infectious disease outbreaks early, supporting the subnational laboratory systems to diagnose resistant and zoonotic pathogens and building a OH workforce to respond to any emerging or re-emerging infectious disease outbreaks.

description.narrative: the purpose of the health financing activity (hfa) is to improve access to equitable and quality health services and prevent catastrophic health expenditure through increased resources for health, efficient allocation and utilization, and enhanced financial risk protection in alignment with ethiopias overall aim of achieving universal health coverage (uhc) through primary health care (phc) by 2035. health care financing reform in ethiopia, initiated in 1998, aimed to improve the quality and equity of health services. the strategy focused on increasing resources for health care, promoting efficiency, and ensuring long-term sustainability through multiple financing mechanisms. key interventions included revenue retention at health facilities, a fee-waiver system, standardized exemption services, and the introduction of health insurance schemes. these reforms have significantly improved health service delivery and financial protection for citizens. usaids investments in healthcare financing reform are largely focused on strengthening and institutionalizing health care financing (hcf) functions and systems to support universal health coverage of quality primary health care (phc) services for ethiopian citizens with reduced financial barriers. the hfa will build upon the lessons derived from previous usaid ethiopia health care financing reform initiatives, including the recent five-year health financing improvement program (hfip). the expected outcomes will be evidence-based and objectively measured through the progress made in the country's capacity to achieve sufficient, equitable, sustainable, and efficient financing for universal healthcare coverage.

The Ethiopia Sustainable Tourism Alliance (ESTA) strives to enhance biodiversity conservation and economic development through sustainable ecotourism products, services and other opportunities in the defined destination regions of the Rift Valley, the Bale Mountains and Awash National Park. A secondary focus is on the mainstreaming of HIV/AIDS prevention and awareness along the tourism value chain in these destinations. While addressing national poverty alleviation concerns outlined in the Plan for Accelerated and Sustained Development to End Poverty, the program also uses an approach to conservation that fully addresses the need to engage neighboring communities. In doing so, ESTA addresses objectives of the U.S. Agency for International Development for both improved natural resource management and conflict mitigation.

description.narrative: The goal of the Communication for Change (C-Change) project in Ethiopia is to integrate mass media, interpersonal communication and community engagement to empower Ethiopian families to take preventive and treatment-seeking actions related to malaria; antenatal care and maternal, newborn and child health; and prevention of mother-to-child-transmission of HIV (PMTCT). C-Change is building on its established working relationships with the Federal Ministry of Health, the regional health bureaus in Oromia and Amhara, nongovernmental organizations, community-based organizations and other partners to improve the effectiveness and sustainability of social and behavior change communication (SBCC) programming. The project is streamlining formative research and pretesting methods and creating easy-to-use, frontline teaching tools and short skills-based training that can be owned and managed by woreda (district) and kebele (municipality) teams. C-Change is strengthening the capacity of regional, woreda and kebele structures to create sustainable SBCC interventions that resonate with target populations and at-risk groups.

(Ethiopia): . USAID aims to strengthen malaria diagnostic capacity at Ethiopian public sector laboratories via technical, strategic, managerial, and operational support in five regions of the country via the Ethiopian Health & Nutrition Research Institute. Activities include: .Review the updating and development of malaria laboratory diagnosis policy guidelines & training materials; Conduct training of health professionals in malaria laboratory diagnosis and quality assessment/quality control (QA/QC); Support the establishment of a QA/QC system for malaria laboratory diagnosis in health facilities including onsite supportive supervision and mentoring; Conduct studies on therapeutic efficacy of anti-malarial drugs and serologyFacilitate the establishment of a national malaria slide bank; Training of trainers of malaria laboratory professionals at Regional Reference Labs...

The TransACTION project targets populations who face a high risk of HIV infection, including commercial sex workers, at-risk youth, mobile and migrant workers, truck drivers and communities along identified transportation routes in Ethiopia. The project aims to provide targeted prevention of new HIV infections; to strengthen linkages to community-based care and support services, HIV counseling and testing, and treatment of sexually transmitted infections for at-risk populations; to increase demand for interpersonal counseling, health services and social support activities; and to improve the capacity of local nongovernmental organizations and private facilities to manage targeted prevention programs.

title.narrative: Ethiopia Comprehensive HIV AIDS Treatement Care and Support Program

description.narrative: The overall goal of this program is to mitigate the impacts of HIV/AIDS in Ethiopia and improve quality of life of PLHIV, their families and the community through sustainable, comprehensive and coordinated evidence based interventions.

The Preventive Care Package (PCP) activity builds upon a solid HIV/AIDS service foundation to address the persistent problem of HIV/AIDS. The activity ensures the prevention care package activities and components are available, acceptable, and sustainable. While physical availability of the kits is an important program component, increasing PLHIV knowledge, skills, and correct utilization on the kit are emphasized by a vast cadre of PCP community workers. Existing health delivery systems are used for the PCP kit distribution and behavior chance communication messaging to build capacity for sustainability and referral to services available outside of the PCP program. The activity directly contributes or refers PLHIV for the following services and support: psychological/mental health; social services; HIV counseling and testing; long-lasting insecticidal nets provision; oral rehydration salts therapy; water, sanitation and hygiene; microfinance; antiretroviral treatment; HIV prevention; nutrition; protective safety net program; deworming; sexually transmitted diseases; and pediatric and orphan and vulnerable children care.

Assist special populations which may be vulnerable or at-risk on a temporary or chronic basis whose needs are not addressed under emergency humanitarian assistance or other programs. These include groups such as the disabled; orphans, children and at-risk youth; victims of trafficking; victims of gender-based violence; refugees, returnees, ethnic minorities, internally displaced or other socially excluded groups; the elderly; and female heads of household. Depending on circumstances, services may intend to protect groups; mitigate adverse conditions they face, or to remove barriers to help integrate them into society. Components may include measures to increase the capacity of local service and advocacy NGOs and/or professional social workers; to establish public/private service delivery partnerships as well as family and community focused service models; to establish effective referral networks; to develop appropriate service protocols and methods for screening prospective recipients; or to improve public understanding and sensitivity to the needs of the vulnerable. While services provided should not exclude victims of trafficking in persons, programs designed specifically for this group fall under the Peace and Security Objective under the Transnational Crime Area and the Trafficking in Persons and Migrant Smuggling Element.

(Ethiopia): In the last year of this HEAL TB award, USAID will focus on sustainability of regional TB programs in program leadership and management, quality DOTS services for early detection and case management, collaborative TB/HIV activities, early detection and management of drug resistant TB and health systems strengthening (HSS). Focus will be given to improving health worker skills; referral linkages; laboratory and diagnostic capacity, including scaling up of GeneXpert diagnosis; drug supply management; M&E; and operations research. In coordination with the MOH and private sector, the activity aims to achieve a TB case detection rate of 75% and treatment success rate of 90%, and to enhance MDR-TB case detection to identify at least 70% of MDR-TB cases and ensure treatment. Activities will be strengthened to achieve 100% HIV testing in TB patients and management of co-infected patients. Support will cover all Amhara and Oromiya regions reaching an estimated population of 54 million.

description.narrative: The goal of the project is to reduce the number of new HIV infections in Ethiopia. The program will support the efforts of GoE in meeting the Strategic Plan for intensifying a Multi-sectoral HIV and AIDS (SPM) II targets of intensifying HIV prevention in Ethiopia.

Under the MULU Prevention II program USAID is helping Ethiopia reduce its HIV prevalence rate by 50 percent by 2015. The program specifically seeks to strengthen HIV/AIDS responses in and around large workplaces in nine regions, especially in the areas of construction, farming and agriculture, leather processing and textile manufacturing.The overall goal of the project is to decrease the number of new HIV infections by reducing risks and vulnerability to new infections through an evidence-based process. The project contributes to the national target of reducing new infections by 50% by 2014.

title.narrative: Reading for Ethiopia's Achievement Developed (READ TA) – Technical Assistance

description.narrative: (Ethiopia): Reading for Ethiopia's Achievement Developed Technical Assistance (READ TA) activity focuses on improving the reading and writing skills of primary school students nationwide. The activity developed a new reading curriculum for grades 1-8 together with the Ministry of Education (MOE). In collaboration with MOE and Regional Education Bureaus(REBs), READ-TA also developed textbooks and teacher's guides in seven mother tongue languages for grades 1-8; and trained 1,200 grade 1-4 teacher trainers.FY 2016 funds will be used to develop English textbooks and teacher's guides for grades 1-8; develop, develop grades 1-8 English teacher training manual; revise preservice English curriculum and build the capacity of MOE, REBs, and CTEs; and train teacher trainers..USAID will develop three additional preservice reading courses. USAID will provide technical assistance to additional mother tongue languages in the adaptation of textbooks and teachers guides.

title.narrative: Pastoralist Resiliency Improvement and Market Expansion (PRIME)

description.narrative: (Ethiopia): PRIME supports resilience among pastoral and agro-pastoral communities, and thus enhances prospects for long-term development through transformative and market facilitation. It focuses on livestock market system strengthening, natural resource management and climate change adaptation, livelihood diversification, enhanced innovation, increasing household decision making power of women, learning and knowledge management, and nutrition promotion. It supports youth through technical and financial skills to start businesses working closely with TVETs in urban centers. The activity also supports the establishment and strengthening of mobile and agent banking platform to offer loans, savings, and money transfer services such as MFIs, saving and credit groups and associations. It will continue to improve market systems and capture lessons learned and will undertake a comprehensive study on pastoral and agro pastoral development to contribute to National Pastoral Policy and Strategy Framework.

description.narrative: (Ethiopia): The Camel Milk Value Chain activity is implemented by a local organization and addresses constraints along the camel milk value chain by improving livestock productivity, addressing quality and hygiene issues, and creating market linkages. The activity conducts training of trainers (TOT) on milk hygiene, camel husbandry, and management to local producers and government workers. It also offers training for animal health, camel husbandry and management to producers, camel herders and pastoralists as well as fodder production and preservation training. In FY 2016, at least 5,000 households will benefit from improved camel dairy production and marketing. The activity supports the commercialization of camel dairy in the Somali region by improving the productivity of camel breeds, strengthening animal health systems, and strengthening market linkages between producers, marketing groups and processing facilities. The majority of beneficiaries are women producers, associations or businesses..

(Ethiopia): The Tigray Youth Association's Promote Environmental Entrepreneurship activity targets 20,000 landless youth and women in four districts of Ethiopia's Tigray Region. To address the increasingly important issues of land shortage and a growing youth (unemployed) population in Ethiopia, the activity uses an innovative approach to engage rural youth in economic activities that also promote land rehabilitation and environmental protection. In FY 2017, the activity will continue to engage youth, including women and girls, in activities such as bee keeping, animal fattening, vegetable and fruit gardening, tree seedling production and planting on rehabilitated communal areas. By increasing youth employment and engagement this activity increases incomes, reduces poverty, and helps to reduce the potential for instability caused by a growing, disaffected youth population.

(Ethiopia): The Strengthening Ethiopia's Urban Health Program (SEUHP) aims at improving the health status of Ethiopia's urban population by reducing the incidence of Tuberculosis (TB), HIV, maternal, neonatal and child morbidity and mortality through improved quality, use, and management of urban health services. The Government of Ethiopia's Urban Health Extension Program engages more than 5,000 nurses to provide household-centered health promotion, disease prevention, and limited curative services in urban areas. In FY 2017, SEUHP will continue to enhance family health, hygiene and sanitation, maternal neonatal and child health services; strengthen health systems in 49 urban areas; train and supervise urban health extension workers; support long and short-term family planning referral services, community-based immunization, HIV testing, anti-natal care referrals and defaulter tracing, postpartum care, and TB screening and referrals.

description.narrative: Support and strengthen the negotiation process and implement peace and reconciliation processes, accords and ceasefire agreements at track levels 1, 2 and 3, including support to indigenous peacebuilding efforts. For a peace/negotiations process to have a chance of success, it must entail building trust in the process, between parties, and among their constituents, with a special focus on including women. Illustrative activities include negotiation training; platform development; public opinion polling; facilitation activities; elder statesmen engagement; provision of international expert advice and knowledge; financial support to parties; multi-stakeholder dialogues; assistance with the design of peacebuilding training programs; support and maintenance of agreed verification mechanisms; support to complaint tracking mechanisms; and work with local and national government representatives to bring them closer to their constituencies.

title.narrative: Improving Reading Skills, Defining Childhood Dreams Project

description.narrative: (Ethiopia): .The Improving Reading Skills activity is implemented by a local Ethiopian non-governmental organization. It focuses on improving the reading proficiency of early grade students in 200 intervention schools of East and West Gojam zones of the Amhara region. The activity is establishing mini-libraries in target schools; providing supplementary reading materials; engaging parents and community members in the promotion of reading competencies; organizing reading clubs; and assisting schools to identify additional time in which students can engage in meaningful reading opportunities. .FY 2016 funds will be used for preparing and distributing 80,000 supplementary reading materials for grades 3 and 4. Funds will also enable technical assistance to school communities on how to strengthen reading corners and clubs. Procurement and distribution of instructional materials for 66 schools that have students with special needs will be another activity which is funded from FY 2016 funds. .

title.narrative: Enhancing the Status of Human Rights Protection and Systems of Good Governance in Ethiopia

description.narrative: (Ethiopia): This activity builds the capacity of Ethiopian judicial and law enforcement authorities to handle cases and improve the quality of justice and enforcement of human rights in Ethiopia. Via the bi-annual Joined-Up Justice Forum, the activity also provides a platform for justice sector and law enforcement professionals to discuss and reach consensus on common issues in connection to their role of interpreting and enforcing the law. In addition, this activity seeks to prevent child marriage and female genital mutilation (FGM) through advocacy. There will be no assistance under this activity to prisons, prison officials, the military or paramilitary forces. Instead, FY 2017 funded interventions will target state actors in the courts, police and community with refresher, advanced training on human rights, particularly for reform-minded officials. These efforts support the GOE's ambitious plan to eliminate child marriage and FGM by 2025.

title.narrative: Local Capacity Building: School and community based malaria communication- Oromia

description.narrative: (Ethiopia): This school and community based malaria communication activity is implemented in the Jimma zone of the Oromia region. The strategies of this activity are to train, mobilize and utilize school communities and communities in targeted high malaria transmission districts. This activity aims to promote the following five key malaria prevention and control practices at the household level: long lasting insecticide nets use; appropriate and timely seeking care for malaria; appropriate use of anti-malaria drugs; and acceptance of indoor residual spraying; and drainage of potential breeding sources around the village

description.narrative: Strengthen the legal, regulatory, institutional, and information environment which protects and enables the growth in associational life and the development of independent and sustainable civil society organizations (CSOs). Build the capacity of civil society organizations to act as agents for reform and support their participation in democratic decision-making through articulating and representing their members interests, engaging in service delivery, and advocating for issues which become part of the public agenda and are reflected in public policies. Encourage the strengthening of a civic culture which supports democratic institutions and processes, active participation in political and civic life, and the civic virtues of tolerance, pluralism, compromise, trust, and respect for individual rights, including gender equality.

description.narrative: Support and strengthen the negotiation process and implement peace and reconciliation processes, accords and ceasefire agreements at track levels 1, 2 and 3, including support to indigenous peacebuilding efforts. For a peace/negotiations process to have a chance of success, it must entail building trust in the process, between parties, and among their constituents, with a special focus on including women. Illustrative activities include negotiation training; platform development; public opinion polling; facilitation activities; elder statesmen engagement; provision of international expert advice and knowledge; financial support to parties; multi-stakeholder dialogues; assistance with the design of peacebuilding training programs; support and maintenance of agreed verification mechanisms; support to complaint tracking mechanisms; and work with local and national government representatives to bring them closer to their constituencies.

title.narrative: Community Based Awareness Raising and Behavioral Change to Reduce Malaria Burden (Amhara)

description.narrative: (Ethiopia): The School and Community Based Malaria Communication activity will train, mobilize and utilize school communities and communities in 36 districts for increased malaria services utilization and uptake in Amhara region. Six districts identified to implement malaria SBC activities with high intensity to achieve 0 indiginous malaria transmission and 30 districts selected to scale up and implement proven malaria communication packages and tools. This activity aims to promote five malaria prevention and control actions namely: Long lasting Insecticide Nets (LLINs) use, appropriate & timely seeking care for malaria, appropriate use of antimalarial drugs, and acceptance of IRS & net care.

title.narrative: Fostering EMA’s Capacity to Promote Continue Professional Development (CPD) and Evidence Based Learning

description.narrative: (Ethiopia): The Ethiopia Medical Association (EMA) program strengthens medical professional development and evidence based learning to improve quality health services. USAID funding supports increased access to standardized Continuous Professional Development (CPD) and evidence-based learning among association members. Major interventions include: establishing and strengthening systems in EMA to institutionalize CPD programs, enhancing joint learning through networking professional associations and their members, and conducting need based standardized CPD in five regions of the country (Addis Ababa, Harari, Amhara, Tigray, and SNNP). In FY 2016, the activity will focus on delivering CPD courses to physicians and other health professionals, preparing additional CPD courses to be delivered face to face and online, continue publishing the Ethiopian Medical Journal online, and continue strengthening EMA and its chapter offices.....

title.narrative: Improving the Health Status of Children through Education and Communication

description.narrative: (Ethiopia): The Organization for Development in Action's (ODA) "Improving the Health Status of Children through Education and Communication" project aims to reduce the incidence of common childhood diseases through Behavior Change Communication (BCC) using community and school approaches. The activity will focus on in- and out-of-school youth in three woredas in Oromia. Implementation activities will include:-Building capacity of health extension workers and teachers in BCC through training/mentorship-Establishing school health clubs -Facilitating community and school conversations-Conducting home visits, and -Developing, producing and disseminating information, education and communication (IEC) materials. The award aligns with the Mission's CDCS DO2, IR2 and with USAID Forward priorities promoting local capacity development and research.

title.narrative: Enhancing the Role of Academia in Evidence Generation for Action in Health Care Financing in Ethiopia

description.narrative: (Ethiopia): The Ethiopian Economic Association (EEA) is a Local Capacity Development (LCD) award to strengthen local capacity to generate and disseminate evidence on Health Care Financing reform (HCFR) implementation and overall health systems in Ethiopia with evaluations and research. With FY 2016 funds, EEA will conduct an evaluation of the GOE's revenue retention and utilization scheme and the impact of free health services on retained revenue and domestic resources mobilization for health care. Findings from these studies will identify challenges and best practices in revenue retention and inform health care finance reform outcomes. EEA also provides capacity building to the EEA association and staff with training and workshops, engages them to complete research and evaluation, and supports members to access and use current HCFR related research and publications...

description.narrative: Support and strengthen the negotiation process and implement peace and reconciliation processes, accords and ceasefire agreements at track levels 1, 2 and 3, including support to indigenous peacebuilding efforts. For a peace/negotiations process to have a chance of success, it must entail building trust in the process, between parties, and among their constituents, with a special focus on including women. Illustrative activities include negotiation training; platform development; public opinion polling; facilitation activities; elder statesmen engagement; provision of international expert advice and knowledge; financial support to parties; multi-stakeholder dialogues; assistance with the design of peacebuilding training programs; support and maintenance of agreed verification mechanisms; support to complaint tracking mechanisms; and work with local and national government representatives to bring them closer to their constituencies.

title.narrative: Afar Community Based Reproductive Health Project

description.narrative: (Ethiopia): Rohi Weddu Pastoral Women Development Organization implements the Afar Community Based Reproductive Health Project in the pastoralist Afar region, an underserved area where USAID had not traditionally worked. The activity will work in five remote woredas of Afar region. It will primarily focus on improving the availability and quality of reproductive health and maternal and child health services by strengthening the health system through training of health extension workers, health workers and woreda health office staff, supporting MCH equipment necessary to provide services and expanding immunization outreach services. The activity uses existing cultural and government structures to improve the utilization of these services to benefit more than 150,000 people, mainly children and women of reproductive age. The award aligns with the Mission's CDCS DO2, IR2 and with USAID Forward priorities promoting local capacity development and research.

title.narrative: Strengthening Malaria Monitoring and Evaluation Systems (SMMES)

description.narrative: (Ethiopia): The Strengthening Malaria Monitoring and Evaluation Systems activity provides the National Malaria Control Program with key technical assistance, operational research, monitoring and evaluation support and data management capacity building. The purpose is to strengthen malaria programming and facilitate implementation of the National Strategic Plan for malaria. Major activities include: .Monitoring and evaluation in the implementation of the national plan.Expanding malaria epidemic surveillance activities.Conducting and coordinating operational research, formative evaluations, and special studies including the malaria indicator survey.Providing carefully-selected technical assistance at national and regional levels in the areas of proposal development, strategic document preparation, and program management
